# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index
   - whether downstream steps depend on pairing semantics
2. Choose an aligner and mode that match the assay instead of reusing a
   familiar default blindly.
3. Treat mapping rate and summary statistics as a sanity check on the
   reference and alignment mode.
4. Apply post-alignment filters deliberately and document what each one
   removes.
5. Accept the alignment branch only if sort order, indexing, and summary
   files all match the delivered BAM.

## Alignment Basics

- **Aligner choice matters**: Different aligners (Bowtie2, BWA, minimap2,
  HISAT2, STAR) have different sensitivity, speed, and intended use

from pathlib import Path
out=Path('/workspace/run_trace/hifiasm_candidates.fasta')
rows=[]

  parts=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
  name,seq=parts[1],parts[2]
  tags={}
  for x in parts[3:]:
   a=x.split(':',2)
   if len(a)==3: tags[a[0]]=a[2]
  L=int(tags.get('LN',len(seq)))
  rd=int(tags.get('rd','-1')) if tags.get('rd','-1').lstrip('-').isdigit() else -1
  circ=name.endswith('c')
  if circ or (13000<=L<=20000 and rd>=20):
   rows.append((rd,L,name,tags))
   fo.write(f'>{name} len={L} rd={rd} tags=' + ','.join(parts[3:]) + '\\n')
   for i in range(0,len(seq),80): fo.write(seq[i:i+80]+'\\n')
rows.sort(reverse=True)
print('selected', len(rows))
for r in rows: print(r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3])

from collections import defaultdict
lens={}
from Bio import SeqIO
for r in SeqIO.parse('/workspace/run_trace/hifiasm_candidates.fasta','fasta'):
    lens[r.id]=len(r.seq)
for mqcut in [0,20,40,60]:
    ints=defaultdict(list); n=defaultdict(int); alnb=defaultdict(int); matches=defaultdict(int)
    with open('/workspace/run_trace/candidates.reads.primary.paf') as f:
        for line in f:
            p=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
            if len(p)<12: continue
            t=p[5]; ts=int(p[7]); te=int(p[8]); m=int(p[9]); alen=int(p[10]); mq=int(p[11])
            if mq<mqcut: continue
            n[t]+=1; alnb[t]+=alen; matches[t]+=m; ints[t].append((ts,te))
    print('MQ',mqcut)
    for t in sorted(lens, key=lambda x:-alnb[x])[:12]:
        L=lens[t]; events=[]
        for a,b in ints[t]: events.append((a,1)); events.append((b,-1))
        events.sort(); cur=last=covered=0
        for pos,delta in events:
            if cur>0 and pos>last: covered+=pos-last
            cur+=delta; last=pos
        ident=matches[t]/alnb[t] if alnb[t] else 0
        print(t,L,n[t],alnb[t],f'{alnb[t]/L:.1f}',f'{covered/L:.3f}',f'{ident:.4f}')
PY"

name: sequence_alignment

# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index
   - whether downstream steps depend on pairing semantics
2. Choose an aligner and mode that match the assay instead of reusing a
   familiar default blindly.
3. Treat mapping rate and summary statistics as a sanity check on the
   reference and alignment mode.
4. Apply post-alignment filters deliberately and document what each one
   removes.
5. Accept the alignment branch only if sort order, indexing, and summary
   files all match the delivered BAM.

## Alignment Basics

- **Aligner choice matters**: Different aligners (Bowtie2, BWA, minimap2,
  HISAT2, STAR) have different sensitivity, speed, and intended use

read-level filtering tasks.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the input facts first:
   - single-end or paired-end
   - read length
   - expected adapters or library type
   - whether the task is trimming, contamination removal, or both
2. Choose the lightest preprocessing that solves the actual problem.
3. Verify that quality improves after trimming instead of assuming it did.
4. If reads are being removed against a reference, define exactly what
   “retained” mean

---
name: sequence_alignment
description: Domain knowledge for short-read alignment and post-alignment processing.
---

# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index
   - whether downstream steps depend on pairing semantics
2. Choose an aligner and mode that match the assay instead of reusing a
   familiar default blindly.
3. Treat mapping rate and summary statistics as a sanity check on the
   reference and alignment mode.
4. Apply post-alignment filters deliberately and document what each one
   removes.
5. Accept the alignment branch only if sort order, indexing, and summary
   files all match the delivered BAM.

## Alignment Basics

- **Aligner choice matters**: Different aligners (Bowtie2, BWA, minimap2,
  HISAT2, STAR) have different sensitivity, speed, and intended use

# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index

   familiar default blindly.

   removes.

   files all match the delivered BAM.

name: sequence_alignment
description: Domain knowledge for short-read alignment and post-alignment processing.
---

# Sequence Alignment

Domain knowledge for aligning short reads to a reference genome and
processing the resulting alignments.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the dataset and assay facts first:
   - read layout
   - assay type
   - reference genome and index
   - whether downstream steps depend on pairing semantics
2. Choose an aligner and mode that match the assay instead of reusing a
   familiar default blindly.
3. Treat mapping rate and summary statistics as a sanity check on the
   reference and alignment mode.
4. Apply post-alignment filters deliberately and document what each one
   removes.
5. Accept the alignment branch only if sort order, indexing, and summary
   files all match the delivered BAM.

events.stdout_excerpt:
convert FASTA/Q to tabular format, and provide various information,
like sequence length, GC content/GC skew.

Attention:
  1. Fixed three columns (ID, sequence, quality) are outputted for either FASTA
     or FASTQ, except when flag -n/--name is on. This is for format compatibility.
  2. The average quality is not the arithmetic average of quartiles (some tools do that).
     How to computate: 1) take the qscore for each base, 2) convert it back to
     an error probability, 3) take the mean of those, 4) and then convert that
     mean error back into a qscore.
     Reference: https://github.com/shenwei356/seqkit/issues/448

Usage:
  seqkit fx2tab [flags]

Created [mitogenome.fasta.gz](/workspace/final_answer/mitogenome.fasta.gz) with exactly one non-empty FASTA record:

- Header: `>Agrius_convolvuli_mitochondrion`

- `gzip -t` passed

Workflow summary: MitoHiFi could not run natively in this environment due a Galaxy container/ptrace failure, so I used the assigned Galaxy history with minimap2, high-depth bcftools mpileup/call, and bcftools consensus to assemble a reference-guided mitochondrial sequence. Details are in [execution.log](/workspace/run_trace/execution.log).
